Situation1: A serious situation has come up in the family, and the grandparent's presence is needed.
Situation2: This is the last weekend before the partner relocates abroad for months.
Story: I stared at my phone, my daughter’s message still glowing on the screen: “Can you come over? We really need you.” My heart clenched. My grandson had been sick all week, and now things had taken a turn for the worse. I knew my family expected me to be there, to comfort, to help, to be the steady presence I always tried to be. But as I set the phone down, I saw the suitcase by the door—my boyfriend’s. This was our last weekend together before he left for his new job overseas. We’d planned every moment, promising ourselves we’d make memories to last until he returned. He was waiting for me in the living room, hopeful, wanting to hold onto these precious hours. I felt torn in two, the weight of both worlds pressing on my chest. My family needed me, but so did he. I could feel their expectations pulling me in opposite directions, and I didn’t know how to choose.
